$comment: G3 (partly answered). Every verification this repository's tooling performs reads material a verifier was HANDED: no linter dereferences a URL, and no check consults live state. That is why `docs/lifecycle-and-custody.md` §1 can say 'unaffected' so often — and it is exactly why custody is the open question, because a verdict is only as durable as somebody's willingness to keep answering the read that supplies the material. This registry names, per verification input, which published operation retrieves it, who serves it, what its absence does to the verdict, and whether that survives a provider exit. An absent input does not have ONE consequence: a required one leaves a stated property unproven and, where a residual rule names it, reported INCOMPLETE; an OPTIONAL opening simply stays unopened; and where a current binding can stand in for a historical one the answer silently becomes a question about today. Each row says which of those it is. Rendered to docs/retrievability.md by scripts/retrievability.py, which also gates it: every retained-material argument of `check_bundle`, every LINT-BND-I* residual and every published as-of read must appear here, so none can be added without saying who keeps it retrievable.

inputs.material: The entity's sealed BW-MED: its provider endpoints and MLS parameters. SBM-ADR-0015 moved the DS receipt keys OFF it, to the provider's own BW-PROVIDER descriptor, and SBM-ADR-0016 says WHOSE descriptor that is: the observing provider's, which the receipt names in its signed `observed_by`. Sealed by a key the DIRECTORY RECORD authorises — the MED is not its own trust anchor.
inputs.absent: the entity's provider endpoints are unknown, so the material they point at cannot be resolved. The MED does NOT pin the other seal keys — `DirectoryRecord.authorized_seal_keys` does — and a retained MED is no substitute for the historical directory authorisation that made it acceptable.
inputs.note: The endpoints INSIDE it move on an exit; the document itself must remain retrievable as it stood at the act, and nothing names who serves that.

inputs.material: The sealed BW-ORG version the message pinned: acceptance policy, delivery grades, scope map.
inputs.absent: the policy that governed the act cannot be read.
inputs.note: Retrieval BY DIGEST is the right interface: evidence pins `acceptance_policy_ref.doc_digest`, so a verifier can ask for exactly the version it needs. The interface is settled; the custody is not.

inputs.material: The BW-ORG succession chain: the versions linking the pinned one to its predecessors, so linkage and in-force at the act can be shown. It does NOT establish that the pinned version was the latest — a retained prefix looks complete whether or not a successor was omitted, which is what LINT-BND-I3 says.
inputs.absent: LINT-BND-I1 / LINT-BND-I3 — linkage and in-force are provable from the pinned document alone; MAXIMALITY is not, and the verdict says INCOMPLETE rather than passing.

inputs.material: The recipient entity's BW-MEMBER bindings as they stand: devices, capabilities, confirmation keys, status.
inputs.absent: no attribution and no satisfiability check can run.
inputs.note: This list answers the PRESENT-tense question only (satisfiability, LINT-BND-08/09). Attribution reads `member_history` as of the act.

inputs.material: Superseded BW-MEMBER versions with their windows, so a member's status and confirmation key can be resolved AS THEY STOOD AT THE ACT.
inputs.absent: attribution falls back to the current binding, which is correct only while nothing has changed; LINT-BND-34 exists because a key minted after the act must not anchor it.
inputs.note: TS ICS 146 / MWAP §3 require as-of retrieval for the evidence retention period, INCLUDING for retired members — a duty on a surface that a provider exit removes.

inputs.material: The SENDER entity's bindings, for the sender half of the identity tuple.
inputs.served_by: the sender entity's provider — a different provider, and often a different jurisdiction
inputs.absent: LINT-BND-I2 — the sender-side half is undecidable from the retained material, reported INCOMPLETE rather than passed or failed.

inputs.material: The sealed ROSTER snapshot for an evidenced epoch: who was in the group, and the ratchet-tree hash.
inputs.absent: membership at the epoch rests on the current roster instead of the one the evidence commits to.

inputs.material: Retained MLS GroupContext bytes for every evidenced epoch, so `mls_state` can be recomputed rather than trusted.
inputs.served_by: the Delivery Service — the retention duty's read surface, access-controlled to authorised verifiers
inputs.absent: LINT-BND-I4 — the state the evidence commits to cannot be inspected, and the verdict says so.
inputs.note: A5, exactly: the READ is published and nothing publishes the BYTES it serves. So this input's gap is the write side, not the retrieval interface — which is the opposite of every other row here, where the interface is settled and only the custody after an exit is not.

inputs.material: The per-device KeyPackage availability and registry revision AS THEY STOOD AT GROUP CREATION, so the cipher-suite decision can be recomputed.
inputs.operation: none published — the read surface exists for group context, not for the formation inputs (A5)
inputs.absent: LINT-BND-I5 — the strongest-usable arm of the suite decision cannot be recomputed.
inputs.note: The registry revision and per-device package availability AT CREATION have no published read at all, so this is a gap one step earlier than `group_contexts`: there is nothing to serve and no way to ask.

inputs.material: The cipher-suite registry revision the formation decision was taken against.
inputs.operation: none published — carried as a demonstration fixture
inputs.absent: the suite decision is taken on trust.
inputs.note: Not a provider's to hold, so an exit does not touch it.

inputs.material: The participant's admission windows, to decide whether each provider named in the evidence was admitted WHEN IT ACTED.
inputs.absent: LINT-BND-I6 — the bundle cannot establish that the providers it names were admitted at the act, and says INCOMPLETE.
inputs.note: The one historical read that a provider exit does NOT touch, because the Authority serves it and is not the exiting party. This is the shape the other rows lack.

inputs.material: The Federation Authority's own seal keys, to verify the register records.

supplied_as.detail: `bundle_lint.py --trust-store` — the verifier's own configured Federation-Authority anchors, not bundle material

inputs.absent: the register is unverifiable, so admission is undecided.

inputs.material: The DS-signed handover receipts the delivery event rests on.
inputs.operation: none published for third-party retrieval — the receipt travels to the party that collected
inputs.served_by: the issuing RDP; the collecting party's own copy

supplied_as.detail: keyed by the delivery it substantiates: the bare `message_id`, or `<origin>/<message_id>` where one identifier is evidenced under more than one origin

inputs.absent: the S2 event rests on the DE's assertion rather than on the DS's signature.
inputs.note: Supplied as a MAP of handle to receipt, not a list: `{"receipts": {"urn:sbm:rdp:mockeu-001/01HZ3AVLBCDEFGH9JKMN0PQRST": "receipt.json"}}`. A BARE key — `{"01HZ3AVLBCDEFGH9JKMN0PQRST": "receipt.json"}` — still resolves, to the one origin this bundle evidences for that identifier; where it evidences several, which delivery is meant is AMBIGUOUS and reported (LINT-BND-I9) rather than settled by the order the evidence was listed in. What the key does is state WHICH delivery the entry claims; it proves nothing about it. The evidence must still establish the origin, the octets and the recipient, and the receipt’s own signed `issuing_rdp_id` is COMPARED with the handle rather than used to choose it — selecting the SE by the claim under test would make that comparison a self-consistency check, which proves nothing about the delivery.

inputs.material: The sealed evidence objects and packages themselves.
inputs.served_by: each party's own wallet copy; the issuing RDP
inputs.absent: there is nothing to verify. A retained DS receipt is related to the delivery it substantiates only through this material — the SE's origin and octet commitment, the evidenced recipient, and at the availability grade the DE's instant. Without them a receipt whose signature verifies may be true about a different delivery, so the relationship is reported UNPROVEN (LINT-BND-I9) rather than passed.
inputs.note: The only material with a SECOND independent holder by design: each party keeps its own copy, so a provider exit does not destroy it. Why the evidence itself is the durable part and the material needed to CHECK it is the fragile part.

inputs.material: The (salt, content_class) opening of an availability-grade commitment.
inputs.operation: none, by design — the salt travels only inside the end-to-end-encrypted envelope
inputs.served_by: the endpoints, and only the parties of a dispute
inputs.absent: the grade commitment stays unopened, which is the point; the claim that rests on it is then unproven rather than failed. That is NOT the same as the class being hidden — a cleartext `scope_ref` resolved against a published scope map can narrow it, and a scope covering one class gives it. What an unopened commitment withholds is the committed value, not every inference about the message.

inputs.material: The opening of an agent act's mandate commitment.
inputs.operation: none, by design — as for reveals
inputs.served_by: the endpoints, and only the parties of a dispute
inputs.absent: the mandate commitment stays unopened, which is the point; the claim that rests on it is then unproven rather than failed. That is NOT the same as the class being hidden — a cleartext `scope_ref` resolved against a published scope map can narrow it, and a scope covering one class gives it. What an unopened commitment withholds is the committed value, not every inference about the message.

inputs.material: Evidence that a Change-Indication Evidence's outputs are the transformation of its input. Neither of the two transformations is profiled, so there is no operation to trace.
inputs.operation: none — neither is profiled (open item A15)
inputs.served_by: nobody: the profile does not claim this is establishable

supplied_as.why: no operation produces the material — neither transformation is profiled (A15) — so no manifest key is defined and none should be

inputs.absent: LINT-BND-I7 — stated as unestablishable rather than reported as a gap in the bundle, because neither is profiled and a provider MUST NOT issue one.

inputs.material: The EU-governed directory record for the entity: where to resolve it, and `authorized_seal_keys` — the set that decides which key may seal its BW-MED/ORG/MEMBER documents.

supplied_as.detail: `discovery_lint.py --directory` — a RETAINED record on disk. The ecosystem retrieval is `GET /resolve/{uid}` at the EDD core registry, but nothing in this repository dereferences a URL: the reference is handed the record, like every other input

inputs.absent: no discovery document can be shown to have been sealed by a key the entity was entitled to use, so the whole discovery chain is unanchored (`check_directory_pin`).
inputs.note: RETR-01 demands the arguments of `check_bundle`, and the trust anchors are arguments of `discovery_lint` instead — which is how this input came to be missing from the inventory. Registry-held, so an exit does not strand it — but the AS-OF question does: the record is served current, and nothing publishes the authorisation as it stood at a past act.

inputs.material: The configured trust anchors a verifier resolves seals against.
inputs.operation: none published — a verifier's own configuration
inputs.absent: no seal resolves to an anchor, so nothing is attributable (`check_trust`).
inputs.note: Held by the verifier rather than by any provider, which is why it survives — and why it is the one input whose absence is the verifier's own problem.

inputs.material: The sealed BW-PROVIDER descriptor of each RDP named in the evidence, carrying the `ds_receipt_keys` that verify its Delivery-Service receipts.
inputs.operation: the provider's own discovery surface; the descriptor's seal key is pinned to the participant by the membership register (LINT-TRUST-07)
inputs.absent: LINT-BND-I8 — the key that signed a retained receipt cannot be resolved, so the handover rests on the DE's assertion alone and the verdict says INCOMPLETE rather than passing.
inputs.note: SBM-ADR-0016 makes the OBSERVING provider's descriptor the one place this key may be published — the receipt names that provider in its signed `observed_by`, and in a four-corner exchange it is the recipient's provider, not the message's origin. SBM-ADR-0015 had moved the key off the customer's BW-MED, where it sat because the Delivery Service was a second provider and the entity's signed document was the only thing already retained for the evidence period. A provider's key belongs in the provider's descriptor — but it moves the key onto a surface a provider exit takes away, where it had been on one the entity controls. That is the trade the decision makes, and this row is where it is visible.
